subject.title: after_tool_call hook receives a flattened string, not the structured ToolResult — plugins cannot detect exec/bash failures

question: Should OpenClaw canonicalize Codex-native shell/apply_patch `after_tool_call` payloads from app-server completion data instead of forwarding Codex's raw string `PostToolUse` response as the plugin-visible result?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the repair changes a public plugin hook payload boundary and must choose between native-relay immediacy, structured app-server fidelity, and duplicate-event avoidance.

options.title: Canonical structured OpenClaw payload
options.body: Use app-server commandExecution/fileChange completion data as the plugin-visible `after_tool_call` result for Codex-native shell/apply_patch and suppress the raw string relay for those tools.

options.title: Wait for upstream Codex payloads
options.body: Keep OpenClaw relay behavior stable and require Codex to emit structured shell/apply_patch `tool_response`, leaving this item blocked until that ships.

options.title: Document raw-string compatibility
options.body: Treat native Codex `PostToolUse` strings as the intended contract and document that plugins must use another surface for exit-code observability.

recommendation.title: Canonical structured OpenClaw payload
recommendation.body: Use app-server commandExecution/fileChange completion data as the plugin-visible `after_tool_call` result for Codex-native shell/apply_patch and suppress the raw string relay for those tools.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a public plugin hook and tool-result middleware boundary decision tied to the merged middleware API scope.
